title: Leadership morning scratchpad — week start
content:
Morning run-down (quick, jot down)

Top objectives this week:
- Shipping canary rollout for 2.1 runtime (gradual traffic shift; watch tail latencies)
- Finalize Dedicated pricing buckets and comms for customers on trial
- Close Private deployment audit checklist + KMS gating for alpha customers

Today (tight):
- 08:30 personal prep: read infra notes, latest perf matrix (see RED-2345)
- 09:00 exec sync (15m) — agenda: 2.1 rollout posture, customer escalations, hiring ask
  - Ask SRE: current 99.9th tail (p90/p95/p99) numbers for GPU pool A vs B
  - Quick decision: enable KV-cache warmup for canary? Pros/cons (risk: small cold-start bump)
- 10:30 infra deep-dive with Tom (30m) — bring list of blockers
  - Follow-ups: Tomas to update autoscaler policy draft (PR #789), check test coverage for fallback paths
- 13:00 customer call: Acme RFP review (prep Qs below)
- 15:00 product council (30m): confirm metric thresholds for Optimize recommendations
- 16:30 wrap + async notes to team

Meeting prep (bullets to bring):
- For Acme RFP: ask about peak qps, inter-region latency SLAs, data residency, audit window (log retention), encryption-in-transit + at-rest expectations
- For infra: what is the expected impact of quantization change on token cost? rough delta request to infra (Ana)
- For Exec sync: hiring ask — senior infra engineer; required start Q2; budget tradeoff vs contractor

Quick numbers (ballpark) — pull reals before 09:00:
- Hosted API avg cost per 1k tokens: ~ $0.85 (target to reduce to $0.72 with batching/quant tweaks)
- Dedicated pool A throughput: 14k tok/s (observed), pool B: 9k tok/s (older GPUs)
- 99th latency for short responses: ~ 210ms (canary currently at 240ms)

Open questions / risks:
- If canary shows p99 > 300ms, fallback policy: auto-shift 20% back to 2.0 model? need Ops sign-off
- Private deployments: KMS integration complexity for on-prem customers — do we ship KMS adapters or require customer HSM? Decide by Thursday
- Sales pressure: three mid-market deals want SLA + dedicated capacity; need legal + infra to confirm commit levels

Action items (to assign quickly):
- [ ] Tom: update autoscaler policy draft and post link (due EOD)
- [ ] Ana: estimate token-cost delta with 4-bit quantization (quick sim) (due Wed noon)
- [ ] Markus: draft customer-facing note on canary rollout and expected impact (due Tue)
- [ ] Me: email legal re: SLA language for dedicated commitments (blocker: termination windows)

Notes to self (voice memo style):
- Keep canary window narrow but measurable — want explicit metrics to roll back within 30m if regressions
- Be pragmatic on GA feature set; remove 'nice-to-have' that increases ops burden before Q2 launch
- Follow up with Ana on cost model used in Optimize suggestions — need a small table for product council

Snippets to paste in meetings:
- "We plan to run a staggered canary for 48 hours with automatic rollback thresholds based on p99 and error-rate. The goal is to minimize user-visible regressions while validating performance gains from batching and kernel updates."
- "For Dedicated customers, we recommend a two-tier commit: baseline reserved capacity + burstable credits. This balances predictable revenue with headroom for spikes."

Random reminders / brain dump:
- Check backfill on hiring pipeline (talent ops) — candidate JDs need tightening (infra senior)
- Add time to review PR #789 (performance): look specifically at fallback logic and metrics emitted
- Confirm we have a single source of truth for per-route costs in Console (token accounting)

End-of-day expected outcomes:
- Autoscaler policy PR updated + link in thread
- Quantization cost estimate from Ana
- Customer note draft by Markus
- Legal reply queued for SLA language

-- LEAH
